title: Update to Google's AI weather model improves forecast accuracy
gist: Google's WeatherNext 3 model now ingests raw satellite data instead of relying solely on reanalysis snapshots, enabling hourly forecasts and measurable accuracy gains over its predecessor and ECMWF's AI model, while still showing black-box artifacts and an unexplained early-forecast weakness.

themes.theme: Architectural shift: raw data over reanalysis

insights.claim: Google's WeatherNext 3 now ingests raw satellite weather data directly rather than relying entirely on 'reanalysis' snapshots, shortening the lag between real-world conditions and a new forecast and enabling hourly forecast updates instead of the prior six-hourly cadence.
insights.speaker: Scott K. Johnson
insights.so_what: Moving from reanalysis-only to raw-data ingestion is a structural upgrade path other AI weather model makers will likely need to follow to stay competitive on forecast freshness.

insights.claim: Nearly all AI weather models to date have trained and operated entirely on reanalyses — globally consistent atmospheric snapshots produced only every six hours — which can lose information present in the original raw data sources.
insights.speaker: Scott K. Johnson
insights.so_what: This describes a known bottleneck across the entire AI weather modeling category, not just Google, implying a broader industry opportunity for raw-data-native architectures.

insights.claim: AI (machine-learning) weather models' core commercial advantage over traditional physics-based models is achieving similar forecast performance while requiring far less computing power, which lets them be run more frequently.
insights.speaker: Scott K. Johnson
insights.so_what: Lower compute cost per forecast run is the economic thesis underpinning AI weather models' displacement of legacy numerical weather prediction infrastructure.
insights.locator: Google is one of the major players

insights.claim: WeatherNext 3 adds a limited amount of physical grounding — checking whether a queried point is land or ocean and factoring in surface elevation — trained on historical weather-station data, to improve calculated surface temperature and dew point at specific locations.
insights.speaker: Scott K. Johnson
insights.so_what: Blending minimal physics-based features into an otherwise black-box ML model is a hybrid design pattern that could generalize to other domains where pure ML underperforms on physically-grounded edge cases.
insights.locator: Unlike traditional models that use physical properties

insights.claim: WeatherNext 3 shows roughly a 5 percent improvement in upper-atmosphere condition accuracy over WeatherNext 2, which Google's team says is equivalent to about six additional hours of accurate forecast lead time.
insights.speaker: Scott K. Johnson
insights.so_what: A ~6-hour lead-time gain is materially useful for downstream commercial users (aviation, agriculture, disaster response) that price decisions off forecast horizon.
insights.locator: They note a roughly 5 percent improvement

insights.claim: WeatherNext 3's new location-specific surface temperature calculation method improved accuracy by up to 30 percent, and the model generally outperforms the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' (ECMWF) AI model on these metrics.
insights.speaker: Scott K. Johnson
insights.so_what: Outperforming ECMWF's AI model on a headline metric strengthens Google's competitive position in the emerging AI weather-forecasting market versus European public-sector modeling.
insights.locator: And their change to calculating surface temperature

insights.claim: WeatherNext 3 is now the underlying source of forecast information across Google Search, Gemini, and Google Maps.
insights.speaker: Scott K. Johnson
insights.so_what: Embedding a proprietary AI weather model across Search, Gemini, and Maps reduces Google's reliance on third-party weather data providers and gives it a distribution advantage that rival forecast vendors lack.

insights.claim: For a number of variables, WeatherNext 3 performs worse than competing models in the initial six-hour forecast window before overtaking them for the remainder of a 15-day forecast, an anomaly the underlying white paper does not attempt to explain.
insights.speaker: Scott K. Johnson
insights.so_what: An unexplained near-term accuracy dip is a real limitation for time-sensitive use cases (e.g., short-notice weather-dependent operations) even as headline multi-day performance improves.

insights.claim: WeatherNext 3's predictions show visible artifacts of its underlying computational grid, such as distinctly hexagonal blobs in precipitation maps, and its ensemble surface-temperature forecasts sometimes produce snapshots where the global average temperature is inconsistently higher or lower rather than staying stable as expected.
insights.speaker: Scott K. Johnson
insights.so_what: Visible grid artifacts and inconsistent global-average outputs are tell-tale signs of the model's black-box nature and a reminder that ML weather models still carry non-physical failure modes physics-based models don't.
